claims.text: Controlled dropwise precursor addition slows the precursor reduction rate relative to continuous addition.
Slower precursor reduction promotes homogeneous alloy formation.
Slower precursor reduction promotes uniformly distributed isolated noble-metal sites.
Homogeneous alloy formation with isolated noble-metal sites enhances catalytic performance.
Noble-metal-based HEA nanoparticles made by continuous precursor addition typically exhibit heterogeneous phase distributions.
Noble-metal-based HEA nanoparticles made by continuous precursor addition typically exhibit variable active-site arrangements.
Controlled dropwise addition reduces precursor mobility.
Controlled dropwise addition reduces the nucleation rate.
Reduced precursor mobility and nucleation rate facilitate more even mixing of the metal components.
Homogeneous alloy formation minimizes phase segregation.
Homogeneous alloy formation produces a higher density of active catalytic sites.
A higher density of active catalytic sites enhances the catalytic reaction rate.
Dropwise addition will yield higher phase purity than continuous addition under otherwise identical conditions.
Dropwise addition will yield a more uniform active-site distribution than continuous addition.
Dropwise addition will yield higher turnover frequencies or reaction-rate constants than continuous addition.
Synthesis below approximately 200 degrees Celsius keeps precursor mobility sufficiently limited for the proposed effect.
The proposed effect should hold within compositional ranges typical of noble-metal-based HEA catalysis.
Mixing dynamics and solvent effects may contribute to the observed catalytic improvement independently of precursor reduction kinetics.
